government.title: When Do Citizens Support Corrupt Politicians? The Trade‐Offs Between Corruption and Competence
government.short_title: When Do Citizens Support Corrupt Politicians? The Trade‐Offs Between Corruption and Competence
government.plain_summary: This research explores why people still support corrupt politicians despite their dislike of corruption in general. It found that when mayoral candidates perform well economically, it helps reduce the negative impact of corruption on public support for those leaders. However, even with competent leadership, citizens value honesty more than competence. Additionally, people who live in areas with less corruption and have lower incomes are less likely to accept corrupt politicians as long as they're competent.

government.title: Do Performance Budgeting Reforms Reduce Corruption? Evidence From a Quasi‐Experimental Study
government.short_title: Do Performance Budgeting Reforms Reduce Corruption? Evidence From a Quasi‐Experimental Study
government.plain_summary: This research looks at whether changing how governments allocate their budgets based on performance results helps reduce corruption. It found that when local Chinese governments started using this new method, they had fewer actual cases of corruption and people thought there was less of it happening too. The study suggests these changes made government spending more transparent and efficient, which helped keep officials from doing things they shouldn't. This research shows how changing the way money is managed can make a difference in preventing bad behavior by those who work for governments.

government.title: Fighting Corruption Through Accountability? A Survey Experiment
government.short_title: Fighting Corruption Through Accountability? A Survey Experiment
government.plain_summary: This research used a survey experiment to understand how different types of accountability—legal, administrative, and social—affect perceptions of corruption among public employees in Taiwan. Despite people correctly identifying the severity of corrupt actions, reminders about these accountabilities didn't improve ethical judgments or encourage whistleblowing. The study found that where someone is placed within an organization can affect how they respond to accountability messages. It suggests that fostering a stronger sense of personal responsibility and ethics might be more effective than relying solely on external controls in fighting corruption.

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.short_title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.source: Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies
government.plain_summary: This paper looks at corruption in Africa by examining how it affects governance, democracy, and mental health. It suggests that corruption is not just a legal issue but also stems from deep social and moral problems left over from colonial times. The study proposes solutions like strengthening institutions, developing ethical leaders, empowering citizens, and using restorative justice methods. By doing this, they aim to improve people's well-being and strengthen democratic systems in Africa.

government.title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fiscal Digitization and E-Procurement Systems in Enhancing Administrative Transparency and Public Sector Integrity
government.short_title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fisca…
government.source: Science, Education and Innovations in the context of modern problems
government.plain_summary: Digital governance in Algeria has been adopted as a strategy to combat corruption, especially in sectors like taxation and procurement. The country is digitizing tax administration and implementing electronic public procurement systems, which have improved transparency and accountability. These digital tools help reduce discretionary practices, enhance traceability, and improve access to information for the public. However, there are still challenges such as incomplete integration of digital systems, cybersecurity issues, and uneven administrative capacity that need addressing.

government.title: Corruption, Governance and the Challenges of the Rule of Law - Law Enforcement and Corruption - An Assessment of the Functioning of the Albanian State Police.
government.short_title: Corruption, Governance and the Challenges of the Rule of Law - Law Enforcement and Corruption…
government.plain_summary: Corruption has been a major issue in Albania for over three decades since its transition to democracy. This corruption spread within national security institutions like the State Police, leading to instability and even threatening their collapse. Efforts by governments have aimed at restructuring and purging corrupt elements from the police force, but political interference continues to be problematic. This undermines law enforcement effectiveness and the credibility of the police force, which is crucial for maintaining a functioning rule of law in Albania.

government.title: Corruption risk indicators in public procurement: Definition and evaluation with organised crime data
government.short_title: Corruption risk indicators in public procurement: Definition and evaluation with organised cri…

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Corrupting U?: Workplace Bullying, Ethical Erosion, and Corruption Contagion in Public Higher Education
government.short_title: Corrupting U?: Workplace Bullying, Ethical Erosion, and Corruption Contagion in Public Higher…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how workplace bullying affects corruption in public universities. It found that when employees are bullied, they're more likely to make unethical decisions and feel less healthy at work. The research also uncovered five main ways bullying leads to corruption: unfair hiring practices, toxic environments, misuse of funds, deception, and discrimination based on race or gender. To prevent this, university leaders need to have strict rules against bullying and must encourage ethical behavior among their staff.

government.title: Bureaucratic Reform to Improve the Integrity of Government Officials as an Effort to Eradicate Corruption and Illegal Levies in Indonesia
government.short_title: Bureaucratic Reform to Improve the Integrity of Government Officials as an Effort to Eradicate…
government.source: International Journal of innovative inventions in Social Science and Humanities
government.plain_summary: To improve governance and reduce corruption in Indonesia, it's crucial to strengthen the culture within government agencies. This involves making sure that all public servants are honest and professional. By doing so, they can better serve the people and implement policies effectively. Building a culture of honesty is key because civil servants who act with integrity help ensure that bureaucratic reforms succeed.

government.title: The Current Situation, Challenges, and Countermeasures of International Cooperation against Corruption
government.short_title: The Current Situation, Challenges, and Countermeasures of International Cooperation against Co…
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: International cooperation against corruption is crucial for tackling cross-border bribery and money laundering. China has established a framework supported by its criminal laws and treaties to facilitate extradition, repatriation, and other measures like persuasion to return. However, challenges remain such as non-extradition of death penalty cases, differences in dual crime determinations, and lack of asset sharing mechanisms. To overcome these issues, it's important to improve domestic legal systems, standardize sentencing procedures, strengthen anti-money laundering efforts, diversify cooperation routes, and enhance judicial assistance protocols.

government.title: How Does Corruption Control Shape Administrative Burden on Businesses? The Moderating Role of Political Attention and Digital Government
government.short_title: How Does Corruption Control Shape Administrative Burden on Businesses? The Moderating Role of…

government.title: Institutional Integrity and Whistleblowing Architecture in Corruption Prevention: A Systematic Literature Review
government.short_title: Institutional Integrity and Whistleblowing Architecture in Corruption Prevention: A Systematic…
government.source: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies
government.plain_summary: This review looks at how organizations can prevent corruption by using frameworks for integrity and whistleblower systems. It found that while there are legal protections against corruption, many people still don't report it because they fear retaliation or lack trust in their organization. The study identified three main areas: understanding why people might not come forward, designing better ways to report issues within the organization, and making sure global rules work together effectively. What's important is having a culture of transparency and strong leadership, rather than just relying on laws.

government.title: The politics of partisan memory: Last letters of anti-fascist resistance in Italy and France (1943–2003)
government.short_title: The politics of partisan memory: Last letters of anti-fascist resistance in Italy and France (…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how political parties in France and Italy used or ignored letters written by people who fought against fascism before they were killed. By examining these letters, researchers found that there was an ethical way to remember these past struggles that could be useful for modern democracies. This approach helps maintain a diverse society rather than just focusing on one group's history. It shows how remembering the fight against fascism can still support today’s pluralistic democracy.

government.title: The Relationship Between Level of Personal Integrity and Anti-Corruption Attitudes among Polytechnic Students
government.short_title: The Relationship Between Level of Personal Integrity and Anti-Corruption Attitudes among Polyt…
government.source: Social Science and Human Research Bulletin
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how much students value their own good behavior and their attitudes towards not doing corrupt things. It involved 111 polytechnic students who answered questions about these topics. The results showed that both personal integrity and the willingness to avoid corruption were quite high among students. There was a strong connection between having good values and wanting to avoid corruption - as one went up, so did the other.

government.title: Fiscal Transparency Deficits and Accountability Failures in South African Local Government: A Qualitative Analysis of Disclaimed Audit Opinions
government.short_title: Fiscal Transparency Deficits and Accountability Failures in South African Local Government: A…
government.plain_summary: This research looked at local government in South Africa and found that many municipalities were not transparent about their finances for several years. Specifically, seven out of 247 municipalities had repeated disclaimed audit opinions from the Auditor-General. The study identified three main reasons: problems with how these municipalities are run (like having too few people or weak controls), issues with leaders following rules, and a lack of trust in government. Understanding these issues can help improve financial management and public trust in local governments.

government.title: The effectiveness of anti-corruption reforms in a region of Europe: the role of social empowerment
government.short_title: The effectiveness of anti-corruption reforms in a region of Europe: the role of social empower…

government.title: Impact Syntheses of Anti-Corruption Technology in E-Procurement and Open Contracting
government.short_title: Impact Syntheses of Anti-Corruption Technology in E-Procurement and Open Contracting
government.source: Research Output Journal of Arts and Management
government.plain_summary: Corruption in public procurement continues to be a significant issue affecting economies and trust among citizens. This study looks at how digital tools like e-procurement systems and open contracting frameworks can improve transparency, accountability, integrity, and fairness in government buying processes. These technologies help reduce opportunities for corruption by making it harder for misconduct to occur. They also make it easier for audits and for smaller businesses to participate.

government.title: BUREAUCRATIC CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC SERVICE DELIVERY IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES AND POLICY INTERVENTIONS
government.short_title: BUREAUCRATIC CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC SERVICE DELIVERY IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES AND P…
government.source: Journal of Management Science and Career Development
government.plain_summary: Bureaucratic corruption is a significant issue affecting how services are delivered by governments in Nigeria. It reduces efficiency, delays projects, and lowers trust from citizens towards the government. Despite efforts to combat it through policies and reforms, corruption still happens at all levels of government across different sectors like health, education, infrastructure, and social welfare. To address this, there needs to be stronger regulation, better training for officials, more citizen involvement in oversight, less political interference, and stricter enforcement of anti-corruption measures.

government.title: Morbidity and Mortality Pattern of Snakebite in Children and Anti-Snake Venom Dose Titration: A Descriptive Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital in South India
government.short_title: Morbidity and Mortality Pattern of Snakebite in Children and Anti-Snake Venom Dose Titration:…
government.source: International Journal of Current Pharmaceutical Review and Research
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how many children get bitten by snakes and what happens when they do. Most bites happen to kids aged 6 to 12 years old, with more boys than girls getting bitten. The most common place for a bite is the leg, especially at night. Sometimes, these bites can cause infections or damage organs like the kidneys.

government.title: Effect of Milk Powder as A Protective Agent on the Stability of Anti-Hp-IgY
government.short_title: Effect of Milk Powder as A Protective Agent on the Stability of Anti-Hp-IgY
government.source: International Journal of Public Health and Medical Research
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how adding milk powder to a special type of egg protein called anti-Hp-IgY can help keep it from breaking down. The study found that when milk powder was added, the egg protein stayed strong even after being exposed to changes in acidity or pepsin, which are substances that can break proteins apart. This means the protective agent (milk powder) helps maintain the effectiveness of the anti-Hp-IgY over time and under different conditions. The findings suggest using milk powder could make it easier to store and use this egg protein as a treatment for infections without needing antibiotics anymore, which is good because antibiotic resistance is becoming more common.

government.title: Editorial: Governance and accountability (Gover-nability) of multiple values of municipal corporations
government.short_title: Editorial: Governance and accountability (Gover-nability) of multiple values of municipal corp…
government.source: International Journal of Public Sector Management

government.title: Ethical Leadership and Public Sector Integrity:Governance Frameworks for Combating Corruption and Rebuilding Institutional Trust
government.short_title: Ethical Leadership and Public Sector Integrity:Governance Frameworks for Combating Corruption…
government.source: International Journal of Administration and Management Research Studies (IJAMRS)
government.plain_summary: This study examines how ethical leadership can improve the trust in government institutions and reduce corruption. It found that leaders who model good behavior are key to creating an honest culture within organizations. Additionally, having strong systems for handling complaints and ensuring accountability is crucial. The research suggests that simply making information public isn’t enough; what matters more is having effective investigation and enforcement capabilities.

government.title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
government.short_title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
government.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
government.plain_summary: This case study examines how a large NGO manages to protect its beneficiaries despite challenges from commercialization pressures. By collaborating with donors, funders, and regulators, the NGO developed new rules and norms for communication between them and beneficiaries. This helped ensure that beneficiary interests were not overlooked. However, cultural differences sometimes prevent full accountability measures being fully effective.

government.title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Government Procurement Process
government.short_title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Gov…
government.source: International Journal of Electronic Government Research
government.plain_summary: This research suggests using blockchain technology to help stop corruption in government buying things. It found that having a good understanding of how to use blockchain is still not common among Thai governments. The study recommends creating new systems with blockchain like smart contracts and online training programs to make sure everyone follows rules fairly during the buying process. This can improve trust between buyers, sellers, and officials.

government.title: CORRUPTION AND ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION IN NIGERIA: A CASE STUDY OF ILORIN-SOUTH
government.short_title: CORRUPTION AND ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT ADMINISTRATION IN NIGERIA…
government.source: GOMBE JOURNAL OF ADMINISTRATION AND MANAGEMENT (GJAM)
government.plain_summary: This research examines how corruption affects local government performance in Ilorin-South, Nigeria. It found that practices like favoritism, ghost workers, and misusing funds significantly reduce the quality of services provided by these governments. The study also showed that having strong accountability measures such as audits, transparent reporting, and citizen oversight can improve service delivery. Overall, the research suggests that corruption deeply impacts local governance negatively, but implementing effective accountability systems can help improve efficiency and public trust in government services.

government.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
government.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

government.title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY IN THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM: THE ROLE OF INNOVATIVE TOOLS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
government.short_title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY IN THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM: THE ROLE…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how digital tools and artificial intelligence can improve anti-corruption efforts in public administration. By using innovative technologies like open data platforms and big data analytics, we can detect corruption risks more proactively than before. However, there are also challenges such as potential biases in algorithms and issues with transparency. The key is to find a balance between letting AI do its work and having humans oversee it properly.

government.title: Financial Development Factors Influencing Corruption Perceptions in European Union Countries
government.short_title: Financial Development Factors Influencing Corruption Perceptions in European Union Countries
government.plain_summary: This study examines how perceptions of corruption are influenced in EU countries by looking at financial inclusion and press freedom. It found that while having more digital banking services can reduce people's perception of corruption, it doesn't have as big an effect as factors like having a free press. A free press leads to greater transparency and accountability, which further reduces corruption views. The research suggests that improving governance structures is crucial for reducing corruption, even with the help of financial technologies.

government.title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.short_title: Corruption in Public Procurement: From Definition towards a Case Study (Part II)
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how to prevent corruption in government buying things and services. It found that businesses often face issues like lack of transparency, dishonesty, and unfair competition when bidding on contracts. The third part looks at how one city handles these processes and suggests ways to make it easier for everyone while saving taxpayer money. By using new technology more, they could help reduce corruption and improve the process.

government.title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption Tool Implementation Methods
government.short_title: Who Acts, and Who is Watched? Differences Between Top-down and Bottom-up AI Anti-Corruption To…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how governments use artificial intelligence (AI) to fight corruption in two ways: top-down and bottom-up. Top-down methods involve government agencies using AI, which can make the process more efficient but might create a cycle where corruption is harder to detect. Bottom-up approaches let citizens participate more directly through AI tools, but they face challenges like limited access to open data. The study suggests that both methods have pros and cons, and there's a need for better integration of citizen participation with AI technology to effectively combat corruption.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.short_title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how Russia is making rules for people to declare if they have done anything wrong that could be seen as corrupt. In recent years, it's gotten more complicated how this works. On one hand, there are now better ways for government to check on people who might be doing bad things and use computers more. But on the other hand, fewer people can easily see these declarations because the government says they need to protect everyone from danger.

government.title: Relevant Issues of Conducting Anti-Corruption Expert Examination of Draft Regulatory Legal Acts by State Authorities of the Subjects of the Russian Federation
government.short_title: Relevant Issues of Conducting Anti-Corruption Expert Examination of Draft Regulatory Legal Act…
government.plain_summary: This article talks about how state authorities in different parts of Russia can check if new rules they're making are free from corruption. It looks at ways to do this effectively and gives examples from other regions. The main idea is to suggest improvements so these checks work better, helping keep laws clean and fair for everyone.

government.title: Navigating the public sector: a quantitative investigation of organisational factors influencing ERP implementation in New Zealand
government.short_title: Navigating the public sector: a quantitative investigation of organisational factors influenci…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study investigates how certain organizational factors impact the successful implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in New Zealand's government agencies. It found that leadership commitment, organizational preparedness, user capability development, and change management readiness are crucial for ERP success. Leadership support was identified as the strongest predictor of ERP deployment success. Interestingly, cultural differences did not significantly affect ERP outcomes.

government.title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.short_title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.plain_summary: E-government has become a way for governments to deliver services more efficiently and make governance transparent. However, implementing it can be challenging, especially in developing countries with limited resources. A case study from The Gambia found that while e-government helps improve service delivery, transparency, accountability, and citizen participation, there are still big hurdles like not having enough IT infrastructure or skilled employees to use digital tools effectively. There's also a lack of collaboration between different government departments and issues related to internet access and trust in government services.

government.title: Does government transparency really matter for citizens’ satisfaction to public service? Empirical evidence from China
government.short_title: Does government transparency really matter for citizens’ satisfaction to public service? Empir…

government.title: AI-ENABLED PUBLIC GOVERNANCE IN DEVELOPING STATES: SERVICE DELIVERY GAINS, ACCOUNTABILITY RISKS, AND A PRACTICAL RISK-BASED REGULATORY MODEL
government.short_title: AI-ENABLED PUBLIC GOVERNANCE IN DEVELOPING STATES: SERVICE DELIVERY GAINS, ACCOUNTABILITY RISK…
government.source: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government
government.plain_summary: Governments are increasingly using AI to improve services like citizen assistance, compliance checks, fraud detection, and planning. These systems can significantly speed up response times and save time for workers. However, without proper oversight, AI can undermine accountability by making decisions harder to understand or challenge, especially in developing countries where institutions might not be fully developed. To address this, a practical risk-based governance model has been proposed.

government.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

government.title: Unethical leadership in the South African public sector tender processes through the lens of game theory
government.short_title: Unethical leadership in the South African public sector tender processes through the lens of g…
government.source: International Journal of Business Governance and Ethics

government.title: Developing a Big Data Strategy: A Public Sector Perspective from the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy
government.short_title: Developing a Big Data Strategy: A Public Sector Perspective from the Ministry of Tourism and C…
government.plain_summary: This study from the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy in Indonesia outlines a strategy for using big data effectively. It uses a method called SWOT analysis and interviews to understand the challenges and opportunities. The goal is to improve decision-making, service delivery, and innovation in tourism and creative economy sectors. By considering governance, technology, infrastructure, and security, they aim to make government operations more efficient and effective.

government.title: Governing AI with trust: an adaptive framework for institutional legitimacy in the UK public sector
government.short_title: Governing AI with trust: an adaptive framework for institutional legitimacy in the UK public s…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how artificial intelligence (AI) is used in the UK public sector and finds that current regulations are not strong enough to build trust. The main issue is that these regulations are not well-coordinated and lack transparency, which can make people feel uneasy about AI decisions. The researchers suggest a new way to think about AI governance that focuses on building trust and coordination among different public sector agencies. They propose a framework that includes having different agencies work together, having independent review bodies, and using metrics that show the AI is fair and trustworthy.

government.title: Real-time Auditing: A Tool to Enhance Good Governance and Accountability for Public Funds
government.short_title: Real-time Auditing: A Tool to Enhance Good Governance and Accountability for Public Funds
government.plain_summary: Real-time auditing is a tool that can help public funds be used more effectively and transparently. It allows for quick insights into how money is being spent and helps ensure that government projects are successful. This is especially important during times of crisis like the pandemic or after financial crises and natural disasters. By providing timely reports, audit offices can help maintain public trust and ensure that government spending is accountable.

government.title: Harnessing Real-Time Analytics for Public Accountability: The Digital Evolution of Supreme Audit Institutions
government.short_title: Harnessing Real-Time Analytics for Public Accountability: The Digital Evolution of Supreme Aud…

government.title: Enhancing Collaboration between Supreme Audit Institution and Anti-Corruption Agencies: Lessons Learnt from Tanzania
government.short_title: Enhancing Collaboration between Supreme Audit Institution and Anti-Corruption Agencies: Lesson…
government.plain_summary: Tanzania is a country with diverse economies including agriculture, mining, and tourism. Despite progress in infrastructure and social services, corruption remains a challenge. Key agencies like the National Audit Office of Tanzania and the Prevention and Combating of Corruption Bureau work together to fight corruption. This collaborative approach has helped improve transparency and accountability.

government.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

government.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
government.plain_summary: This working paper discusses how corruption is not just about individual bad behavior but a networked issue involving social, economic, and political interactions. Understanding these networks can help in fighting corruption more effectively by seeing how they function across different levels of society. By looking at the structures and norms that support corrupt activities, we can develop better strategies to combat it. The paper suggests that anti-corruption efforts should learn from informal networks' positive aspects, making them a useful model for new initiatives.

nonprofit.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
nonprofit.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

nonprofit.title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.short_title: Recent Expansions in Anti-Microbial Profile of Quinoline Analogues: A Review
nonprofit.plain_summary: Recent research has shown that adding different parts called heterocyclic systems to quinoline molecules can create compounds with many useful properties. These modified quinoline-based drugs are effective against a wide range of harmful bacteria, including those causing serious infections. They also show promise in treating cancer and other conditions like seizures, pain, inflammation, and heart problems. By combining quinoline with other parts, scientists can make new medicines that work better than existing ones.

nonprofit.title: Measuring Compliance Maturity and Organizational Integrity: A Conceptual Framework for an Integrated Governance and Ethics Model
nonprofit.short_title: Measuring Compliance Maturity and Organizational Integrity: A Conceptual Framework for an Inte…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how organizations measure their compliance with rules and regulations. Many existing models focus mainly on following the rules, but overlook important aspects like leadership commitment to ethics and overall organization strength. To address this, they propose an integrated model called CGMM that considers both governance (how decisions are made) and ethical practices together. This helps in better understanding how well organizations handle compliance while also ensuring strong values and integrity.

nonprofit.title: Lack of “severe or pervasive” misconduct sinks employee claim
nonprofit.short_title: Lack of “severe or pervasive” misconduct sinks employee claim
nonprofit.plain_summary: In a recent case, an employee claimed they were discriminated against due to their disability but lost the lawsuit because there wasn't enough evidence showing severe or widespread misconduct by their employer. This means that proving discrimination often requires more than just one isolated incident; it needs substantial proof of repeated bad behavior from management. Practically speaking, this highlights the importance for employers to maintain a fair and consistent workplace environment free from serious misbehavior, as even minor issues can be used against an employee's claims in court if they are trying to prove discrimination.

nonprofit.title: Value-Based Drivers of Humanitarian Donation Intentions in a Muslim Context: The Moderating Role of Religiosity
nonprofit.short_title: Value-Based Drivers of Humanitarian Donation Intentions in a Muslim Context: The Moderating Ro…
nonprofit.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research examines how personal values influence people's willingness to donate to humanitarian causes in Aceh, Indonesia—a region known for its generosity. It found that altruistic, social, and emotional values, along with the reputation of organizations, strongly impact donations. Interestingly, religiosity plays a crucial role by amplifying these effects, making people more likely to commit to donating over time. For NGOs working in this context, understanding how different religious beliefs influence giving can help them tailor their fundraising strategies better.

nonprofit.title: BUREAUCRATIC CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC SERVICE DELIVERY IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES AND POLICY INTERVENTIONS
nonprofit.short_title: BUREAUCRATIC CORRUPTION AND ITS IMPACT ON PUBLIC SERVICE DELIVERY IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES AND P…
nonprofit.source: Journal of Management Science and Career Development
nonprofit.plain_summary: Bureaucratic corruption is a significant issue affecting how services are delivered by governments in Nigeria. It reduces efficiency, delays projects, and lowers trust from citizens towards the government. Despite efforts to combat it through policies and reforms, corruption still happens at all levels of government across different sectors like health, education, infrastructure, and social welfare. To address this, there needs to be stronger regulation, better training for officials, more citizen involvement in oversight, less political interference, and stricter enforcement of anti-corruption measures.

nonprofit.title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
nonprofit.short_title: Multi-Actor Collaboration and NGO Accountability: An NGO Case Study
nonprofit.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
nonprofit.plain_summary: This case study examines how a large NGO manages to protect its beneficiaries despite challenges from commercialization pressures. By collaborating with donors, funders, and regulators, the NGO developed new rules and norms for communication between them and beneficiaries. This helped ensure that beneficiary interests were not overlooked. However, cultural differences sometimes prevent full accountability measures being fully effective.

nonprofit.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
nonprofit.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
nonprofit.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
nonprofit.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

nonprofit.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
nonprofit.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

nonprofit.short_title: Working Paper 57: Mapping and strengthening the evidence base for anti-corruption Collective A…

nonprofit.plain_summary: This working paper offers a new way to understand how different groups like businesses, non-profits, and governments can work together more effectively against corruption. It includes tools that help researchers, practitioners, and policymakers compare various anti-corruption efforts and see what works best in different places. By understanding how these collaborations impact real-world changes in preventing corruption, it helps design better partnerships to make a difference.
